newsitem.title: BULGARIA: ELEVATOR BOMB KILLS BULGARIAN INSURANCE OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: ELEVATOR BOMB KILLS BULGARIAN INSURANCE OFFICIAL.

text.p: An official from a Bulgarian insurance company was killed and two other people were injured by a bomb planted in an apartment elevator on Thursday in the Black Sea port of Varna, national radio said.

The radio quoted local police as saying Yordan Markov of the private Security Insurance Company (SIC) died instantly and a 19-year old girl and a Georgian citizen, who were also in the elevator, were wounded.
Bulgaria's crime rate has soared since the collapse of the communism in 1989 as the country grapples with its transition to market economy.
Bombings are a common method of settling scores between shady rival business groups, some of which are said to operate under the guise of insurance companies. SIC has always denied racketeering.
The radio quoted police as saying they did not know whether the bombing was related to Markov's work for SIC or to his own private business.
SIC officials were not immediately available for comment.
On Wednesday, a bomb exploded in the car of a lawyer working for businessman Ivo Karamanski. No one was hurt.

Unknown assailants planted a bomb last month in the car of a senior official who is chief liquidator of a Bulgarian bank and a member of the country's Central Electoral Committee. The official was not hurt in the blast.
